deep.reconstruction:
Context: bundle 'Primzahlen'. The previous page deals with products over primes, prod(1-1/p), and d log Pi(x)/dx. This page is a short exercise on rearranging the conditionally convergent alternating harmonic series, then a generalisation to 1/sqrt(n) and to an arbitrary f.

(1) Setup. Riemann first strikes out '1+1/2+1/3'. He then writes the odd reciprocals 1, 1/3, 1/5, 1/7 in one row and -1/2, -1/4, -1/6 below them, grouped so that two positive terms go with one negative term. He records
  log 2 = 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - 1/4 + 1/5 - 1/6 + ...
and the rearranged series
  (1/2) log 8 = 1 + 1/3 - 1/2 + 1/5 + 1/7 - 1/4 + 1/9 + 1/11 - 1/6 + ...,
that is (3/2) log 2.

(2) First trial: the ordinary order.
  sum_{n=1}^m 1/(2n+1) - sum_{n=1}^m 1/(2n).
He rewrites this with harmonic numbers H_k = sum_{n<=k} 1/n:
  sum_{n<=2m+1} 1/n - 2*(1/2) sum_{n<=m} 1/n = H_{2m+1} - H_m = 1/(m+1) + 1/(m+2) + ... + 1/(2m+1).
He uses H_k ~ log k + C, so this is about log(2m+1) - log(m+1), which tends to log 2.
[My note: for the identity to hold exactly, the odd sum must start at n=0, i.e. include the term 1.]

(3) The rearranged series, partial sum after 3m terms (2m positive, m negative).
  sum_{n=1}^{2m} 1/(2n-1) - sum_{n=1}^m 1/(2n)
  = [H_{4m} - sum_{n=1}^{2m} 1/(2n)] - sum_{n=1}^m 1/(2n)
  = (1/2)(2 H_{4m} - H_{2m} - H_m).
As m tends to infinity, the bracket behaves like 2 log 4m - log 2m - log m = log 8 (implicit step mine). Riemann writes this as (1/2)(log 2 + log 4) = (1/2) log 8 = (3/2) log 2.

(4) The same experiment with 1/sqrt(n).
  sum_{n=1}^m 1/sqrt(2n-1) - sum_{n=1}^m 1/sqrt(2n)
  = sum_{n=1}^{2m} 1/sqrt(n) - 2 sum_{n=1}^m 1/sqrt(2n).
The last form equals sum_{n<=2m} n^{-1/2} - sqrt(2) sum_{n<=m} n^{-1/2}. Its limit is (1 - sqrt(2)) zeta(1/2) = eta(1/2) (identification mine). A coefficient written before the second sum in the first line is unclear.

The line just under the rearranged log 8 series, read by the transcriber as '= 1/sqrt(1.2) - 1/sqrt(2.3) + 1/sqrt(8) - 1/sqrt(4)', is probably the start of the alternating 1/sqrt(n) series. It is illegible and not fully consistent.

(5) General scheme.
  f(1) - f(2) + f(3) - f(4) + ...
  = lim [ sum_{n<=m} f(2n-1) - sum_{n<=m} f(2n) ]
  = lim [ sum_{n<=2m} f(n) - 2 sum_{n<=m} f(2n) ].
With f(n) = n^{-s} this is the device behind sum (-1)^{n-1} n^{-s} = (1 - 2^{1-s}) zeta(s).

Purpose. The page seems to be an exploration of how the value of a conditionally convergent series depends on the order of its terms. It also reduces alternating sums to plain partial sums of sum f(n). This is relevant to the conditional-convergence questions that arise with prime products and series, and with zeta-type series on or near s = 1/2.
errors: In step (2) the lower index of sum 1/(2n+1) should be n=0 (or the term should be 1/(2n-1)) for the identity with H_{2m+1} - H_m to hold exactly; minor slip.
The final line '=1/2(log 2 + log 4' is an asymptotic limit, not an equality of finite sums; the Euler-constant terms cancel (2C - C - C = 0), which is left implicit but is correct.

The line under (1/2)log 8, transcribed as '=1/sqrt(1.2) - 1/sqrt(2.3) + 1/sqrt 8 - 1/sqrt 4', is not consistent as written; it is likely a garbled or abandoned start of the 1/sqrt(n) alternating series.
The coefficient before the second sum in the first 1/sqrt line is unclear; the correct identity requires a plain minus sign (coefficient 1), as the following line confirms.

results.what: Rearranging 1 - 1/2 + 1/3 - ... as two positive terms then one negative term gives (3/2) log 2 = (1/2) log 8
results.modern_name: Rearrangement of the alternating harmonic series (illustration of the Riemann series / rearrangement theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1837) for this example; general theorem to Riemann (Habilitationsschrift 1854, published 1867)

results.what: Evaluation via harmonic numbers: H_{2m+1} - H_m -> log 2 and (2H_{4m} - H_{2m} - H_m)/2 -> (1/2) log 8
results.modern_name: Asymptotics of harmonic numbers, H_n = log n + gamma + o(1)

results.what: Alternating sum f(1) - f(2) + ... = lim [sum_{n<=2m} f(n) - 2 sum_{n<=m} f(2n)], applied to f = n^{-1/2}
results.modern_name: Dirichlet eta / zeta relation, eta(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s}) zeta(s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine scratch work on rearranging the alternating harmonic series, a topic Riemann is already famous for (the rearrangement theorem in his 1854 Habilitationsschrift). The example itself is Dirichlet's. The eta/zeta reduction is classical. The only mild interest is seeing this material in the prime-number bundle, next to the 1/sqrt(n) case.

checkable.sympy: limit((2*harmonic(4*m) - harmonic(2*m) - harmonic(m))/2, m, oo) - log(8)/2
checkable.asserts: The partial sums of the 2-positive/1-negative rearrangement tend to (1/2) log 8 (expected result: 0).
The finite identity used in step (3) holds exactly (expected result: 0).
The finite identity for the 1/sqrt(n) case holds (expected result: 0).
The limit of the alternating 1/sqrt(n) series is eta(1/2), approximately 0.6049.

transcription_corrections: The first sum in step (2) is sum_1^m 1/(2n+1) as written, but the identity with H_{2m+1} - H_m needs the term 1, i.e. a lower index of 0.
The struck '[-sum-]' before sum_1^{2m+1} is a crossed-out symbol; the coefficient is '2*(1/2)', i.e. 2 * sum 1/(2n) rewritten as sum 1/n.
'log 2m+1 - log m+1 = log 2' should be read as log(2m+1) - log(m+1) -> log 2.
In 'sum_1^{2m} 1/(2n-1)' the upper limit 2m is written over a corrected symbol, and the denominator appears overwritten (2n+1 corrected to 2n-1).
The line '= 1/sqrt(1.2) - 1/sqrt(2.3) + 1/sqrt 8 - 1/sqrt 4' is doubtful and only partly legible; possibly an attempt at 1/sqrt1 - 1/sqrt2 + 1/sqrt3 - 1/sqrt4.
The final 'log 2 =' under the (1/2) log 8 line is a marginal label next to the derivation.
'f(1) - f(2) + f(3) - f(4)': the first two arguments are smudged in the image but clearly 1 and 2.
